title: Yehudah Ish Chotzi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yerushalmi Sheviit, chapter 5, halakhah 5, relates that he secluded himself in a cave for three days to consider why the lives of the people of his own city take precedence over those of another city. Rabbi Yosi ben Chalafta came to him. Rabbi Yosi summoned his son R' Avirdomas, and he explained the reason to him. In [Nedarim, chapter 11, at the end of halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.11.1.7), a scribal error has crept in. In any case, I have already explained in the entry Isi ben Yehudah how the Yerushalmi should read.[^1]

notes.text: שנטמן means that he secluded himself in the cave. וקרא means “summoned,” and בריה specifies the son. The pronouns in “he explained the reason to him” follow Hyman’s wording. סה״א means the end of halakhah 1; the final first-person cross-reference is Hyman’s own.

The parallel in Yerushalmi Nedarim 11:1:7 calls the summoned son Rabbi Abba rather than Avirdomas, and describes the arrival differently. Hyman attributes a scribal error to the Nedarim text but gives no corrected name in this notice.

At the boundary between printed pages 552 and 553, ט״ס (“scribal error”) is followed by מ״מ, וכבר בארתי. Here מ״מ is מכל מקום, “in any case.” The Hebrew transcription instead has מ״ם, which could be read as “the letter mem.”
